pr_title: Skeleton rest fixer: Apply orthonormalized scale to anims
pr_body:
Adjust the logic for position and scale animation tracks in the Apply Node Transforms case To match how we adjust bone pose/rest, use basis.orthonormalized() for parentless bones.

Fixes #91893 
Cc @TokageItLab @fire

issue_context.title: [4.3] Mesh disappears when importing an AnimationLibrary onto a GeneralSkeleton
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

* Reproducible in 4.3-dev6
* Not reproducible in 4.2.2.stable

### System information

Windows 11, geForce 4080, Godot 4.3-dev6, Forward+

### Issue description

I have an anim library I've applied a bone map on and an armature with mesh I've also applied a bone map on. Both are taken from mixamo. When I create an inherited scene from the mesh GLB, add an animation player and import my anim library in 4.2, things work exactly as they should. The same process in 4.3-dev6 causes the entire mesh to disappear.

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/334808/cc2059e5-3e67-4cf0-921c-230870e05be7)


Example video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Ob5M0YIgQs

### Steps to reproduce

- Have a character and some animations downloaded from mixamo. Mine are in an anim library.
- Apply a bone map with default settings to both the character and anim library.
- Create inherited scene from the character GLB. Add an animation player
- Load the AnimationLibrary into the anim player

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Godot 4.2.2 project: [TestMixamo42.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/15290104/TestMixamo42.zip)
Godot 4.3-dev6 project: [testmixamo43d6.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/15290105/testmixamo43d6.zip)

In both:
* Open Main.tscn
* Click on the AnimationPlayer and load the animation library
comments:
Bisect points to #90064 as the culprit:

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/44306054/b39d7b91-dd9d-4535-af6f-1df79ff31407)
I think this is an intended behaviot rather than a bug. Is the Hips scale track you intended? If you don't need it, enable the remove unimportant track option.

Oh sorry I, the scale track is not removed with that option.

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/61938263/144081e7-e19c-4d33-80ec-5457e0f51efb)

So, do we need an additional option to remove the scale track? Also, I am wondering what the scale track is on the software that created the glb. We need to determine if there is a problem with the scale track conversion (Apply Node Scale) or if the animation is oddly to begin with on DCC.
For the mesh I downloaded the fbx from mixamo, imported into the latest Blender, changed nothing and immediately exported as glb with default options - just the animation checkbox unchecked.
I, @TokageItLab and @lyuma are looking into this.

Thank you for providing the reproduction project for4.2.x. I can confirm that the issue is also present in that version (tested on 4.2.1) when Remove Immutable Tracks is unchecked.
![godot_scaled_skeleton_4 2](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/39946030/ac050e79-93b0-4097-8755-4009a6ada517)

The reason Remove Immutable Tracks concealed the problem in 4.2 is it removed all tracks that had only one keyframe if the initial pose was the same as the keyframe.

The problem is that after applying Apply Node Scale, the Scale track values mismatch with the Skeleton's rest.

Even in 4.2.1, Remove Immutable Tracks did not specifically hide the problem, but guaranteed that the rest would match the Skeleton Node, so removal there made sense.

Since https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90064, Remove Immutable Tracks is now done after Apply Node Scale, so the comparison needs to be changed.

@lyuma The current importer process matches which of the following flows? Or other?

1. Override Rest -> Fix Silhouette -> Apply Node Scale -> Remove Immutable Tracks
2. Override Rest -> Fix Silhouette -> Remove Immutable Tracks -> Apply Node Scale
3. Apply Node Scale -> Override Rest -> Fix Silhouette -> Remove Immutable Tracks

If Remove Immutable Tracks is running after Apply Node Scale, there are two possible fixes.

- Move Remove Immutable Tracks before Apply Node Scale
- Apply Node Scale to all keys in the scale track

Probably the former should be chosen, since the latter could corrupt the animation if the bones have scale intendedly as glTF. But considering the role of retargeting in matching the appearance, the latter may be preferable, then we need to be careful if the glTF specification allows such cases as Scale of 0.

Probably #3.
It is incorrect to remove tracks before the retargeting flow. We need to be able to compare against the bone rest. The reason is because animation mixer may use bone rest as the reference point when no explicit reset animation exists (and indeed, when the user requests creating a RESET animation, it is based on the bone rest)

> Move Remove Immutable Tracks before Apply Node Scale

This is incorrect, because it will remove things that match the old bone rest which will then lead to incorrect blending after we change the rest.

I strongly believe that this bug is unrelated to Remove Immutable Tracks. It only appeared to be related because remove immutable was incorrect previously


> Apply Node Scale to all keys in the scale track

This is kind of what I am trying, but the code is written to only touch the toplevel bones (get_parentless_bones)

review_comments:
Do we need to orthonormalize the transform or just the basis? Like so:
```suggestion
										anim->track_set_key_value(i, j, (global_transform.basis.orthonormalized() * sc).get_scale());
```
To be honest, I am not sure. The point is that this calculation should be identical to line 136, where they also wrote it this way.
Looking at the code in `Transform3D` it's identical, wasn't sure if there was some unnecessary computations done in the `Transform3D` method so it's equivalent

I assume this is not a valid solution for bones that are intentionally scaled as glTF, as there is no guarantee that this is normalized. Apply Node Scale processes the scaling by Node, but not the scaling that Bone has.

I think there is a guarantee that glTF bones exported from Blender will be scale normalized but it is not for all glTF.

So, if we do this, wouldn't we need to process the Apply Node Scale to set the Scale of all bones to 1?

Why would it be invalid for scaled bones? global_transforms is the global scale adjustment propagated from nodes, and that is what is being orthonormalized. The point of Apply Node Transforms is to make these transforms identity. The code is not orthonormalizing `sc`, so it will still apply any non-uniform local bone scale animation tracks.

if your assertion is that this code is wrong, then line 136 (set_bone_pose_scale) would also be wrong. But I would need to see a test case

~I think line 136 is correct, but the code to apply own scaling (to normalize all bone scale to 1) to each bone is lacking. Also, I think the code for the scale track around line 200 is wrong: the position track is scaled, but the scale track should be multiplied by the inversed scale as `key_value = key_value * (1.0 / scl)`.~

This could be a misunderstanding. Indeed, it is possible that 136 is wrong in the first place.

However, at the very least, it should be true that Apply Node Scale does not currently set the rest of each bone to 1.0.

For test cases, you have tested only:

```
Skeleton: scale = (0.01, 0.01, 0.01)
L Hips: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
  L Spine: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    L Chest: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
```

So, the following should be tested:

```
Skeleton: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
L Hips: scale = (0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
  L Spine: scale = (0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
    L Chest: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
```
```
Skeleton: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
L Hips: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
  L Spine: scale = (0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
    L Chest: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
```
```
Skeleton: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
L Hips: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
  L Spine: scale = (2.0, 1.0, -1.0)
    L Chest: scale = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
```

I guess the only restriction on the bone scale that glTF has is orthogonal. So I expect that scale(0, 0, 0) would not be acceptable, but something like scale(0.001, 0.001, 0.001) or scale(1, 2, 1) would be acceptable.

This may be uncommon, but it is a possible use case.

Suppose we have a model with a neck rest scale of 0.001 for headless-able model like Dullahan, and an animation key value with a pose scale of 1.0 for the neck with a head for retargeting. If the rest scale of the neck is set to 1.0, then the animation key value should be 1000.0.

> Suppose we have a model with a neck rest scale of 0.001 for headless-able model like Dullahan, and an animation key value with a pose scale of 1.0 for the neck with a head for retargeting. If the rest scale of the neck is set to 1.0, then the animation key value should be 1000.0.

Ah, I missed that this is the PR to do that. If so, this change may be correct. But I think that the option "to force REST to 1.0" needs to be added later separetely from this PR as an enhancement to match the look of modification by the animation; This relates to issue https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/84249. Now SkeletonModifier will allow us to implement BoneConstraint in 4.4, so some workarounds for per-bone scaling could be implemented in Godot --Perhaps it would be better to implement a module like BoneExpander as a simpler modifier for scaling.

However, apart from this, I am wondering if the past remove immutable tracks are dead code due to the #90064 change, are they still being used for something other than Skeleton?
Are you aware of the difference between orthonormal (uniform scale) and orthogonal (non uniform scale) methods on basis?

Yes, I assume the glTF restriction is orthogonal without isotropic (means allows non-uniform scale), but please point out if I'm wrong. However, I am getting a bit off-topic.

I think we need to make a new proposal on how to handle individual bone scales.
